prayerExcerpt.en-US: It is in vain that we take the name of Christians, or pretend to follow Christ, unless we carry our crosses after Him.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: É em vão que tomamos o nome de cristãos, ou pretendemos seguir a Cristo, a não ser que levemos as nossas cruzes após Ele.

meta.face: Two clearly different young men of Palestine with warm olive-brown skin. ADRIAN (left): about thirty, with a COMPACT, ROUND-TOPPED head and a BROAD, SHORT face — PROMINENT, round, high cheekbones, a SHORT, broad nose with a slightly flattened tip, narrow, dark almond eyes that turn up at the outer corners, thick, straight black brows, a wide, full mouth; short, tight black curls; a SHORT, ROUNDED black beard; his gaze bold, toward us. EUBULUS (right): about twenty-two, with a LONG, THIN, bony face — a high, narrow forehead, a LONG nose with a pronounced HUMP, large, soft, dark eyes under softly arched brows, lean cheeks, a small mouth, a LONG, narrow chin; straight black hair falling over the forehead; only a faint DOWN of first beard on the lip and chin; his gaze gentle, turned toward Adrian.
meta.basis: No likenesses survive. The Painter's Manual gives Adrian 'a young man with a rounded beard' and Eubulus 'an incipient beard', and the card follows both. The book's engraving shows two haloed men seized at the city gate by soldiers; the gate and Caesarea's harbour (Wikipedia) are the background. The face structures are our choice.
